question.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{12}$ be I.I.D. random variables with probability density function

$$
f(x;\theta )=(\theta +2){x}^{-\theta -3},\,x\ge 1,
$$

where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter. For a particular sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{12},$ you're given that 

$$
{\prod }_{i=1}^{12}{x}_{i}=12.1.
$$

Find the likelihood function of the sample.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=12$ independent random variables with unknown parameter $\theta ,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=(\theta +2){x}^{-\theta -3},\,x\ge 1.
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}((\theta +2){x}_{i}^{-\theta -3}) \\  & =(\theta +2)^{n}\cdot {\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{-\theta -3} \\  & =(\theta +2)^{n}({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i})^{-\theta -3}\end{aligned}
$$

We are told that ${\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}=12.1$ and $n=12.$ Therefore, 

$$
L(\theta )=(\theta +2)^{12}(12.1)^{-\theta -3}.
$$
